tests.title: Unit 4: Books of Second Entry – Ledger – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: A ledger is:
options: A book containing all accounts, where transactions from the journal are classified under account heads
questions.explanation: It is the principal book of accounts.

questions.question_text: The ledger is called a book of final entry because:
options: Entries are finally posted into accounts here from the journal and subsidiary books
questions.explanation: Journal is the book of original entry.

questions.question_text: The ledger is called the "king of books" because:
options: It contains all accounts and is the main source for final accounts
questions.explanation: Trial balance and final accounts are prepared from it.

questions.question_text: A feature of a ledger is that it:
options: Classifies transactions account-wise and contains a separate page for each account
questions.explanation: Each account has debit and credit sides.

questions.question_text: Ledgers are classified into:
options: Debtors' ledger, creditors' ledger and general ledger
questions.explanation: The general ledger holds other accounts.

questions.question_text: A private ledger contains:
options: Confidential accounts like capital, drawings and profit and loss
questions.explanation: It is kept by the owner or a trusted person.

questions.question_text: The format of a ledger account has:
options: Two sides (debit left, credit right), each with date, particulars, J.F. and amount
questions.explanation: The T-format is used.

questions.question_text: In a ledger, "To" is used on the _____ side and "By" on the _____ side:
questions.explanation: "To" for the debit side and "By" for the credit side.

questions.question_text: A journal folio (J.F.) is:
options: The page number of the journal from which a posting is made
questions.explanation: It helps cross-reference.

questions.question_text: The journal differs from the ledger in that the journal is a:
options: Book of original entry in date order, ledger is a book of final entry account-wise
questions.explanation: Journal records chronologically; ledger classifies.

questions.question_text: Posting is:
options: Transferring entries from the journal to the ledger accounts
questions.explanation: Each entry is posted to the debit and credit accounts.

questions.question_text: The first step in posting a journal entry is to:
options: Open an account for each head and write the date and particulars on the proper side
questions.explanation: Then record amount and folio.

questions.question_text: In posting a compound entry:
options: Each debit and credit account is posted separately to its own account
questions.explanation: Total debits must equal total credits.

questions.question_text: Balancing an account means:
options: Finding the difference between the totals of debit and credit sides
questions.explanation: It is done at the end of a period.

questions.question_text: The balance of an account is found by:
options: Totalling both sides and taking the difference
questions.explanation: The larger side minus the smaller side.

questions.question_text: "By balance c/d" is written when:
options: The debit side is greater than the credit side
questions.explanation: It is entered on the credit side to equalise totals.

questions.question_text: "To balance c/d" is written when:
options: The credit side is greater than the debit side
questions.explanation: It is entered on the debit side.

questions.question_text: "Balance b/d" means:
options: Balance brought down to the next period
questions.explanation: It is the opening balance.

questions.question_text: Accounts that normally have debit balances are:
questions.explanation: Debtors, cash, purchases, rent.

questions.question_text: Accounts that normally have credit balances are:
questions.explanation: Creditors, capital, sales.

questions.question_text: A cash account:
options: Cannot have a credit balance as cash paid cannot exceed cash available
questions.explanation: A credit balance would indicate an error.

questions.question_text: At the year end, nominal accounts are:
options: Closed by transfer to the trading or profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Their balances are not carried to the next year.

questions.question_text: Cash A/c: Capital 1,00,000 received; paid furniture 20,000, rent 2,000; received from Shyam 24,000; paid Ram 29,000; drawings 5,000. Balance is:
questions.explanation: Receipts 1,24,000 − payments 56,000.

tests.title: Unit 4: Books of Second Entry – Ledger – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: Shyam's account: sold goods 25,000; returns 1,000; received 20,000; discount 400. The balance is:
Purchases 30,000, 20,000, 15,000, returns 5,000. Net purchases balance is:
Sales 50,000, 40,000, returns 4,000. Net sales balance is:
Rent paid 1,000 per month for 6 months; outstanding 1,000. Rent transferred to P&L is:
Salary paid 10,000 and 10,000; outstanding 5,000. Salary transferred to P&L is:
Bank A/c: deposit 50,000; cheque issued 20,000; withdrew 5,000; cheque received 10,000. Balance is:
Furniture A/c: bought 30,000; sold 10,000 (cost). Balance is:
Discount allowed: 200 + 300 + 150 + 350 = ?
questions.explanation: Total discount allowed is a loss.

questions.question_text: Discount received: 100 + 150 + 250 = ?
questions.explanation: Total discount received is a gain.

questions.question_text: On Jan 1 the entry Cash Dr 50,000 to Capital 50,000 is posted. In the ledger, Cash A/c has:
questions.explanation: Capital A/c gets "By Cash 50,000".

questions.question_text: Rent paid 2,000; outstanding 500; received 1,000. Net rent expense is:
Opening entry: Cash 10,000; Stock 20,000; Debtors 15,000 / Creditors 12,000; Capital 33,000. Total debit is:
questions.explanation: Assets 45,000 = liabilities 12,000 + capital 33,000.

questions.question_text: Ledger balances are carried forward by:
options: Writing the balance c/d and bringing it down as b/d in the next period
questions.explanation: Real and personal account balances continue.

questions.question_text: A nominal account is closed at the year-end by:
options: Transferring its balance to the P&L (or trading) account
questions.explanation: Expenses are credited, incomes are debited when closing.

questions.question_text: A trial balance is:
options: A statement of debit and credit balances of ledger accounts on a given date
questions.explanation: It checks arithmetical accuracy.

questions.question_text: An objective of a trial balance is to:
options: Check the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger
questions.explanation: It also helps prepare final accounts.

questions.question_text: The methods of preparing a trial balance are:
options: Total method, balance method and total-cum-balance method
questions.explanation: The balance method is most common.

questions.question_text: In the balance method:
options: Only the balances of accounts are listed
Totals of both sides are listed
questions.explanation: Debit balances in one column, credit balances in the other.

questions.question_text: In the total method:
options: Totals of debit and credit sides of each account are listed
questions.explanation: It does not give balances.

questions.question_text: The total-cum-balance method shows:
options: Both the totals and the balances of accounts
questions.explanation: It combines the two methods.

questions.question_text: The format of a trial balance has columns for:
options: Account name, L.F., debit amount and credit amount
questions.explanation: Totals must agree.

questions.question_text: Opening stock appears in the trial balance:
questions.explanation: It is an asset carried forward.

questions.question_text: If closing stock is given in the trial balance, it is:
options: Shown on the debit side (as an asset) and not in the trading account's credit side again
questions.explanation: It is an adjustment already recorded.

questions.question_text: Debtors appear in a trial balance:
questions.explanation: They are assets.

questions.question_text: Drawings appear in a trial balance:
questions.explanation: They reduce capital.

tests.title: Unit 4: Books of Second Entry – Ledger – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: Bank overdraft appears in a trial balance:
questions.explanation: It is a liability.

questions.question_text: The provision for doubtful debts appears:
options: On the credit side of the trial balance
questions.explanation: It is a provision (liability or contra-asset).

questions.question_text: Cash 5,000; Capital 40,000; Purchases 30,000; Sales 45,000; Rent 2,000; Furniture 18,000; Creditors 10,000; Debtors 25,000; Drawings 5,000; Discount allowed 500; Salary 9,500. The trial balance total is:
questions.explanation: Debits: 95,000; credits: Capital 40,000 + Sales 45,000 + Creditors 10,000 = 95,000.

questions.question_text: Debit total 2,50,000 and credit total 2,35,000. The difference of Rs 15,000 is:
options: Placed on the credit side as suspense account
questions.explanation: The suspense account balances the trial balance.

questions.question_text: Which error is NOT disclosed by a trial balance?
options: Error of omission (complete omission of a transaction)
questions.explanation: Others: errors of principle, compensating errors, errors of commission with equal effect.

questions.question_text: Which error is disclosed by a trial balance?
options: Posting an amount on one side only
questions.explanation: One-sided errors disturb the agreement.

questions.question_text: Agreement of a trial balance does not prove complete accuracy because:
options: Some errors do not affect the equality of debits and credits
questions.explanation: E.g., errors of principle.

questions.question_text: Compensating errors are:
options: Errors that cancel each other's effect, e.g., one account overcast by 100 and another undercast by 100
questions.explanation: The trial balance still agrees.

questions.question_text: An error of principle is:
options: Wrongly treating the nature of an item, e.g., treating furniture purchase as expense
questions.explanation: Capital versus revenue confusion.

questions.question_text: Errors of omission are:
options: Transactions completely or partially omitted from the books
questions.explanation: Complete omission does not affect the trial balance.

questions.question_text: Errors of commission are:
options: Errors in recording or posting, e.g., wrong amount or wrong account
questions.explanation: They arise from carelessness.

questions.question_text: A suspense account is:
options: A temporary account to record a difference in the trial balance until the errors are located
questions.explanation: It is closed when errors are rectified.

questions.question_text: A trial balance differs from a balance sheet in that the trial balance:
options: Lists all ledger balances to check accuracy, and is not a financial statement
questions.explanation: The balance sheet lists assets and liabilities only.

questions.question_text: A limitation of the trial balance is that it:
options: Does not prove complete accuracy as certain errors are not revealed
questions.explanation: It only proves arithmetical equality.

questions.question_text: The trial balance helps prepare final accounts by:
options: Providing all ledger balances in one place
questions.explanation: Final accounts are built from it with adjustments.

questions.question_text: The correct order is:
options: Ledger, journal, trial balance, final accounts
Final accounts, trial balance, ledger, journal
Journal, ledger, trial balance, final accounts
Trial balance, journal, ledger, final accounts
questions.explanation: Record, classify, summarise, report.

questions.question_text: A trial balance is prepared at the end of the period because:
options: All transactions have been posted and balances can be extracted
questions.explanation: It is a summary of the ledger at a date.

questions.question_text: If the trial balance does not tally, the first step is to:
options: Check the totalling and balancing, then posting from the books
questions.explanation: Then trace the difference.

questions.question_text: A difference of Rs 90 in the trial balance suggests:
options: A transposition or slide error (difference divisible by 9)
questions.explanation: 90 is divisible by 9.

questions.question_text: If the difference is exactly divisible by 9, the suspected error is:
questions.explanation: E.g., 45 written as 54.

questions.question_text: If the difference equals twice an amount, the suspected error is:
questions.explanation: The amount was posted on the wrong side.

questions.question_text: A slide error is:
options: Shifting of digits to the left or right, e.g., 420 written as 4,200
questions.explanation: A transposition error is reversing digits, e.g., 54 written as 45.

tests.title: Unit 4: Books of Second Entry – Ledger – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: Suresh (creditor): purchased 15,000; returned 1,000; paid 10,000; discount 300. Balance is:
Commission Received A/c: received 2,000 and 3,000; accrued 500. Transferred to P&L:
Interest Paid A/c: paid 4,000; outstanding 1,000. Transferred to P&L:
Insurance A/c: paid 12,000; prepaid 3,000. Transferred to P&L:
Drawings A/c: cash 6,000; goods 2,000; interest on drawings 300. Total drawings is:
Opening stock of 20,000 and closing stock of 35,000: in the trading account, opening stock is shown on the _____ and closing stock on the _____:
questions.explanation: Closing stock also appears on the asset side of the balance sheet.

questions.question_text: In a two-column cash book, the two money columns are for:
questions.explanation: Discount columns make it three-column.

questions.question_text: Capital 50,000 cash; purchases 20,000 cash; sales 30,000 cash; wages 3,000. The cash balance is:
Bought goods for 10,000 on credit from A; returned 2,000; paid 7,000. Balance in A's account is:
A debit balance in Debtors account is transferred to:
options: The asset side of the balance sheet
questions.explanation: It appears as sundry debtors.

questions.question_text: In the total method, an account shows:
options: The total of the debit and credit sides in the trial balance
questions.explanation: Each account appears with both totals.

questions.question_text: A posting error on one side only will:
options: Make the trial balance totals disagree
questions.explanation: Debits will not equal credits.

questions.question_text: A Furniture A/c has debit side total 45,000 and credit side total 5,000. The balance is:
questions.explanation: The debit side is larger.

questions.question_text: An Outstanding Salary account with credit 6,000 and debit 6,000 has:
questions.explanation: The liability is cleared.

questions.question_text: The closing balance on the Capital account represents:
options: The owner's claim on the business at the end of the period
questions.explanation: It appears on the liabilities side of the balance sheet.

questions.question_text: The ledger balances of assets and liabilities:
options: Appear in the P&L account only
questions.explanation: Nominal accounts go to the P&L.

questions.question_text: "Balance b/d" in the cash account at the start of the next period is:
options: The closing cash balance of the previous period
questions.explanation: Brought down as the opening balance.

questions.question_text: Folio columns are used for:
questions.explanation: They help trace entries both ways.

questions.question_text: Debtors and creditors are kept in separate ledgers in large businesses to:
options: Divide work and ease control and checking
questions.explanation: It allows specialisation.

questions.question_text: A ledger differs from a ledger account in that a ledger is:
options: A book containing all accounts, a ledger account is a single account in it
questions.explanation: The book versus the account.

questions.question_text: The general ledger containing nominal and other accounts is also called the:
questions.explanation: It contains all accounts except debtors and creditors.

questions.question_text: A control account is:
options: A summary account for a group of accounts, e.g., all debtors
questions.explanation: It verifies the accuracy of the subsidiary ledger.

questions.question_text: The ledger:
options: Can be maintained without any source
Cannot be maintained properly without the journal (or subsidiary books) as the source
questions.explanation: Entries come from the journal or subsidiary books.

questions.question_text: An advantage of computerised ledgers is:
questions.explanation: Also easy retrieval and automatic posting.

questions.question_text: Debit balances total Rs 5,68,000 and credit balances Rs 5,60,000. The suspense account is:
questions.explanation: Credits are short, so suspense is credited.
